title: Capacity Planning and Cost per Request
summary: Turn traffic into a GPU count and a bill. This lesson derives per-GPU capacity from the batching model, sizes a fleet for peak load with target utilisation and redundancy, and computes cost per million tokens, per request and per useful answer, including the build-versus-buy break-even.
objectives: Estimate one GPU's sustainable requests per second from prefill and decode time
Compute GPUs needed as ceil(peak load / (per-GPU capacity x target utilisation)) and add redundancy
Compute cost per million tokens, per request and per useful answer, including the effect of utilisation and retries
Find the break-even between a hosted API and self-hosting
Choose the levers (caching, quantization, routing, batching) that reduce cost most for a given workload
prerequisites: This lesson combines the whole module: latency metrics ([Measuring Inference](/learn/inference-and-serving/measuring-inference)), the memory-bound decode model ([Where the Time Goes](/learn/inference-and-serving/memory-and-compute)), batching ([Batching and Scheduling](/learn/inference-and-serving/batching)), quantization and caching.
